findings.evidence: 'P(like) — immediate resonance', 'Pattern interrupt: break expectations', and 'Short sentences. Punchy.' illustrate the dominant content: familiar engagement and copywriting advice. The algorithm primer and optimization framework add little expert knowledge beyond what the model already knows.
findings.fix: Compress familiar signal definitions and generic style guidance into brief activation cues. Spend the remaining space on non-obvious trade-offs, such as when a provocative reply hook undermines the standalone value needed for reposts.

findings.evidence: 'Optimize across these dimensions:' introduces six parallel objectives, while '**RECOMMENDED:** [which version + any hybrid suggestions]' supplies no method for resolving conflicts between reply volume, repost value, and negative-signal risk.
findings.fix: Add a prioritization framework: establish the audience and communication goal, identify the source's strongest supported payoff, choose the engagement objective that serves that goal, and recommend the variant whose benefits outweigh its trust and negative-signal risks.

findings.evidence: 'Never trigger:' lists spam, manipulative engagement bait, rage bait, and 'Cringe'. These are mostly familiar taste warnings, with little causal explanation and no concrete gotchas distinguishing legitimate links or questions from counterproductive bait.
findings.fix: Replace subjective warnings with concrete failure conditions and reasons. Explain why withholding the entire payoff makes a post bait rather than standalone value, why unrelated questions produce low-value replies, and when removing a launch link would defeat the user's actual goal.

findings.evidence: 'description: Transform a raw tweet idea into an optimized viral post for X' identifies the task and platform, but leaves implicit trigger scenarios and drafting-versus-publishing boundaries unspecified.
findings.fix: Rewrite tweet ideas and drafts into three X/Twitter post options with engagement analysis and a recommendation. Use when asked to improve a tweet, sharpen an opening hook, make an announcement more shareable, or turn a rough topic into a post. Drafting only; not publishing, scheduling, or guaranteeing reach.

findings.evidence: 'Avoid low-arousal states: sadness, contentment, boredom' imposes a blanket emotional prescription despite the later instruction to 'Match the author's authentic voice while amplifying it'. There is no escape hatch for intentionally quiet or reflective material.
findings.fix: Default to the author's intended emotional register. Treat higher-arousal framing as an optional technique only when compatible with the topic, audience, and requested tone; explicitly allow restrained or reflective variants.

findings.evidence: Reading commands/evals/viral-tweet.json returned 'ENOENT: no such file or directory'; commands/evals/ contains explain-pr-changes.json and files/, but no eval file for this command.
findings.fix: Add commands/evals/viral-tweet.json with realistic rewrite prompts and expected outputs, including empty arguments, an underspecified topic, and a fact-sensitive launch announcement. Assert the three distinct variants, preservation of supplied facts, compliance with the requested length, and appropriate clarification when essential information is missing.

findings.evidence: The example input says only 'We just launched our new product after 6 months of work', but the endorsed output asserts 'we deleted our codebase and mass-resigned the team' and 'the product that almost killed us'. Following this example introduces unsupported events and stakes.
findings.fix: Replace the example with a rewrite grounded solely in the supplied launch and six-month timeline. Explicitly prohibit inventing metrics, team events, personal experiences, or dramatic stakes; ask for supporting details before adding them.

findings.evidence: 'Provide:' leads directly into the output template. The numbered optimization dimensions are criteria, not an ordered workflow, and there is no draft-validation-revision loop or check that the proposed posts fit the intended length.
findings.fix: Add ordered phases: collect the idea and constraints, draft the three variants, check each against the requested post length and output requirements, revise failures, then recommend a version. Default to a standard 280-character post unless the user specifies a different format.
